subject: Pilot connection budget playbook & quota next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Chen <alex@finpulse.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot SLOs & connection budget — recap + asks

Alexandra / Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap and proposed asks so we have a single source of truth before we draft a pilot offer. TL;DR: FinPulse is targeting a low-latency streaming scoring path with sustained concurrency and a brief, high-volume burst window.

Key notes from the call:
- Latency target: p95 <= 180–220ms for short scoring requests (~64–256 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained ~35–45 req/s during business hours; 3x short bursts during peak events (up to ~140 req/s for ~30s).
- Concurrency: real-time streaming sessions ~120–160 concurrent WebSocket sessions; up to 300 parallel non-streaming requests across backend pool.
- Connection pattern: clients will use long-lived WebSocket sessions from ~5 app servers; each app server may multiplex 20–40 logical streams per socket.
- Durability: need request-level audit logs + per-request IDs retained for 30 days.

Asks / action items for Redwood (please confirm):
1) Can we provision a pilot with a dedicated connection budget to guarantee the 120 concurrent streaming sessions and the burst envelope?
2) What are the per-connection and per-tenant rate limits you would apply (defaults vs. pilot exception)?
3) Can Redwood support websocket multiplexing (N logical streams per TCP socket) or do we recommend separate sockets per stream?
4) Please share a preliminary rate/quoting sheet (tokens / connections / burst pricing) for review.

Attachments: conn_requirements.xlsx (traffic by endpoint + latency targets)

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood to share a short technical note and a draft rate proposal (Monica / Marissa to own).
- FinPulse to share sampled traffic trace (CSV) and confirm internal app server count.
- Schedule pilot kickoff next week if numbers align.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Monica’s note by EOD tomorrow.

—
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-13T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLOs & connection budget — recap + asks

Thanks Dylan — this is helpful and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 120–160 concurrent streaming sessions is our steady-state target for the West coast region; global footprint later. We want to guarantee no more than 250ms tail latency for those streams (p99 ideally).
- During product demos/marketing events the burst may go higher; please include a configurable burst token bucket (we don't want to over-commit but want a safety margin).

Samir and I attached our traffic extract (finpulse_traffic.csv) with session durations and arrival patterns. Couple asks from procurement side:
- Will Redwood allow a short-term pilot with an uplifted connection quota (30 days) without long-term commit?
- We need a clear statement on how rate limits are applied (per-api-key vs per-tenant vs per-ip).

Thanks — Samir and I are available for a quick follow-up on Monday to go over the draft pricing.

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-14T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLOs & connection budget — recap + asks

Alexandra — thanks for the traffic extract, that was very helpful. A couple of notes from an implementation and pilot perspective, plus a short proposal attached (rate-proposal.pdf).

Technical clarifications and recommended approach:
- WebSocket multiplexing: Redwood supports logical multiplexing over a single websocket connection for streaming—this is enabled by default on our SDK. For your pattern (5 app servers × ~30 logical streams each) we recommend 1–2 sockets per app server to maintain headroom and simplify health checks.
- Connection budgeting: for the pilot we can provision a dedicated connection quota of 200 concurrent logical streams (pilot window), with capability to burst to 450 using a token-bucket configured at the tenant level (burst window 60s).
- Rate limit model: apply limits at the API key (tenant) level for token-generation throughput; also enforce soft per-socket limits to prevent noisy neighbors. For the pilot we recommend: tenant_concurrent_streams: 200 (guaranteed), tenant_burst_capacity: 450 (best-effort), per_socket_max_streams: 50.
- Latency SLOs: given your traffic shape, we can target p95 < 220ms for 64–256 token scoring and p99 < 400ms under guaranteed capacity. Achieving p99 < 250ms will require higher reserved GPU capacity (we can show cost delta in the proposal).
- Observability: we'll wire per-request tracing and provide a dashboard that breaks down token latency, queueing time, and kernel time. Logs retained 30 days as requested.

Commercial / pilot proposal highlights (see attached PDF for full numbers):
- Pilot term: 30 days, non-recurring commitment for quota testing.
- Pilot pricing: nominal pilot fee + usage overage at standard hosted rates.
- Dedicated quota uplift: one-time configuration for tenant connection guarantees (no infra changes required on your side).

Attachments: rate-proposal.pdf (draft numbers + cost delta table)

Next steps I suggest:
1) Dylan to confirm pilot acceptance and preferred kickoff slot.
2) FinPulse to approve pilot quota and sign short pilot addendum (we can issue an abbreviated DocuSign).
3) Monica + Marissa to run a pre-kickoff checklist (traffic replay, keys, dashboard access).

Let us know if you'd like us to lower the initial guaranteed quota and run a staged ramp instead — we can do 100 -> 200 -> 400 as telemetry looks good.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Pilot: 30 days, guaranteed tenant_concurrent_streams: 200, tenant_burst_capacity: 450 (60s window).
- Pricing: see attached draft; pilot fee covers configuration and extended logging.
- Operational: Monica will run the checklist; Marissa will provision dashboard and credentials.

- Send an abbreviated pilot addendum for signature via DocuSign.
- Lock in a kickoff slot next Tue/Wed (we have a 9–11am PST and 2–4pm PST slot open).
